title: Where to Listen

serves.summary: The learner puts an ear where a far-away tap, an underwater click or a call can be heard, which shows that sound travels through air, water and solids and that what it travels through matters.

request.topic: Sound travels through air, water and solids
request.objective: Sound travels through air, water and solid things, and how well it gets to a listener depends on what it travels through: a far-away tap carries along a metal or wooden rail but not along hay, clicks under water are heard under water, and a call in the air is heard in the air. NGSS 1-PS4-1 (SCI001-03-a)

problems.ask: Your friend taps the post very softly, far away. Put your ear where you can hear the taps.
problems.goal: The ear is pressed to the metal rail: the tap travels along the metal to the ear. In the air, a soft tap from that far is too quiet.

problems.ask: Your friend clicks two stones under the water. Put your ear where you can hear the clicks.
problems.goal: The ear is under the water: the clicks travel through the water. Very little of the sound gets out of the water into the air.

problems.ask: Your friend taps the post very softly again. Put your ear where you can hear the taps.
problems.goal: The ear is pressed to the wooden rail: wood carries the tap. The hay bales soak it up, and the air is too quiet from that far.

problems.ask: Your friend calls out from across the pond. Put your ear where you can hear the call.
problems.goal: The ear is in the air: the call travels through the air. Under the water, very little of a sound made in the air gets in.
